task.title: Keep generated Roleplay openings as beat briefs
task.source: Live inspection of Scene: Everybody Gets Ice Cream on the Pi.

coreClaim: New generated Roleplay scenes cannot pass a near-complete planner-written response into the Roleplay writer as the planned opening beat.
rootCause: The scene planner defined firstMessage as narration-style prose with no size boundary, so the Narrator Guide supplied the writer with a second, nearly complete response that overrode the intended fresh prose behavior.

inScope: Focused regression proof for the planner-to-writer contract
outOfScope: Changing character cards, presets, providers, Conversation, or Game
Guaranteeing subjective prose quality across every model

claimBoundary.coreClaim: The planner supplies a compact beat brief rather than a finished opening response.
legacyPathsOrFormats: Existing saved scene openings and prompt snapshots

contractLaneGate.brokenContract: A planning value described as intent was allowed to become a full competing prose sample.
contractLaneGate.impliedContract: The planner chooses the opening situation and the Roleplay writer realizes it using current scene and style context.
contractLaneGate.actualEnforcement: The planner requests a one-to-three-sentence beat brief and the scene service sentence-bounds overlong output to 360 characters.
contractLaneGate.primaryOwnerDetail: The Roleplay scene service owns scene-plan semantics.
contractLaneGate.wrongLaneFixToAvoid: Do not add another universal anti-AI prose instruction or patch provider output after generation.
regressionProof: The focused test captures the planner request and requires the beat-brief contract.
The same test returns an overlong scripted plan and proves the persisted firstMessage is bounded before writer consumption.
Existing multiline normalization coverage proves short planner text remains unchanged.

positiveRows.claim: An overlong planner-written opening is reduced to a compact beat.
positiveRows.evidence: scene-service.spec.ts returns the ice-cream-style four-sentence plan and requires firstMessage <= 360 characters.

positiveRows.claim: The planner is explicitly asked for planning intent rather than finished prose.
positiveRows.evidence: The captured LLM system request contains compact beat brief, not finished prose and the no-scripted-dialogue rule.

contradictionRows.claim: Short valid planner messages must not be rewritten by the limiter.
contradictionRows.evidence: Existing double-escaped multiline regression remains byte-for-byte green after the conditional limiter fix.

legacyDefaultRows.evidence: No storage migration or existing-record update is included; enforcement occurs only while planning a new scene.

untestedRows: Subjective output quality across every writer model
Live newly generated scene behavior before exact merge-SHA images are deployed

ownedFacts.description: The live ice-cream scene's Narrator Guide contained nearly the complete final response as its planned opening beat.
ownedFacts.evidence: Pi prompt preview showed the long scripted ice-cream allocation and dialogue inside Narrator Guide immediately beside the matching generated reply.

verification.baselineCommand: pnpm vitest run src/engine/modes/roleplay/scene/scene-service.spec.ts; pnpm typecheck; pnpm check:architecture; pnpm check; git diff --check
verification.baselineEvidence: 42 focused scene-service tests, pnpm typecheck, pnpm check:architecture, git diff --check, and full pnpm check passed; unused-code output remained warning-only.
negativeRowsTested: Overlong finished-prose opening cannot pass through unchanged
Short multiline planner text remains unchanged

notes: Private roleplay text is summarized in proof language and is not copied into the repository.
Production deployment must wait for the exact merge revision's matched server and web image batch.
